question: What is the user feedback on the Essential PH-1 camera?
answer:
One reviewer wrote that the camera feedback was a big concern before buying, but after receiving the phone three updates were immediately available so the low light issues and slow shutter speed challenges never appeared. [e48515a4a172_1]
That same reviewer said the new portrait feature was put through the paces and is a great feature with solid results. [e48515a4a172_1]
One reviewer listed the camera as needing a lot of improvement and said the magnetic 360 Camera takes a long time to open the dedicated camera app and settings. [b0739227ff49_0]
One reviewer said the camera and its supporting software is only average compared to any other stock Android experience, but that using the Pixel Camera App improved picture quality substantially. [b02b6a8fa5d9_0]
One reviewer said that with Gcam on the final Oreo build the phone often produces very good photos, provided the lighting is decent enough. [c0a143c6613c_5]
One reviewer reported that within two weeks the PH-1 camera stopped working and that Essential declined support because the phone was bought from a reseller. [a7ad34b085de_0]

chunks.text: As a former owner of all of the larger device manufacturers (Motorola, LG, HTC, Apple, etc.), the customized OEM "skin" have yielded little benefit other than expedited battery drain. Essential staying with a stock Android UI allows the PH-1 to operate very fast, hold a charge for almost 2 days with moderate use, and supports honest multi-tasking. Like you, the camera feedback was a big concern for me. The camera reviews received little love, and from what I read, this was deserved. However, when I received the phone, 3 updates were immediately available so the low light issues and slow shutter speed challenges never appeared. In fact, last night I received another camera update. The new portrait feature has been put through the paces on the phone and is a great feature with solid results.

The Essential Ph-1 is an amazing device that I would recommend to anyone with realistic expectations. If you want more than 128gb of storage and a headphone jack in lieu of a full screen display and high end build quality, there are many options available at a significantly higher cost.

Essential Phone PH-1 Full Written Review. Okay today what I have for everyone is my full written review on the essential phone ph1. I divided this review into categories that I think are important to consider before your making purchase. That being said I hope everyone finds this helpful and let's begin. 1. Build Quality and Design- talking about the build quality and design. I have to say essential did a great job there's no rattling or creaking of any kind all the buttons give me a nice tactile and clicky feedback when pressed. The combination of glass and ceramic building materials feel very good in hand and overall the device has a nice solid weight to it. The biggest downside to the overall build quality and designesign is however that those build material choices make the device very very slippery.

essential ph-1 is subtly elegant piece of technology. The essential ph-1 is subtly elegant piece of technology. The android OS works fast and smooth. It fits excellent in the hand and is a perfect replacement to my Nexus 5x. I have switched between multiple different devices this past month to find a permanent replacement under 500 for my previous phone and so far this seems to be it. I'm looking forward to essential home device when it is launched.

UPDATE: with Gcam on the final Oreo build, it often produces very good photos, provided the lighting is decent enough. I hope my rather lengthy review could help you in your decision... so, all in all, even with the small issues I had, I can wholeheartedly give the PH-1 5 stars. Another PSA on replacement parts availability: Currently, Essential doesn't sell any replacement parts for it's phone, so GET A CASE! The phone is rather slippery on the back, and tends to slide off flat, slightly angled surfaces (like a tiling ledge in the bath room... ). I heard though that Essential is pretty nice on replacing the whole phone if you pay a small sum. UPDATE, 16.07.2018: Another update, after half a year of ownership.

PH-1 Android Is Been Great So Far.. Essential Phone in Halo Gray: PROS: a very great built phone, the softwares are instant as the Google Pixel, Futuristic Design, almost can't even notice that there is a small notch up top of the PH-1, speakers are pretty loud, screen is pretty bright, quite responsive touch too. CONS: with the new Android P: the PH-1 has been a little annoying at times, not all the apps are compatible to support the notch due to which apps take half the screen size which means I get to see less content, some minor software bugs and fixes needs to be rolled out instantly (added securities and refinement to new and old features), the camera needs a lot of improvement, the magnetic 360* Camera takes a long time to open the dedicated camera app and settings.

The folks at Essential have done a great job at addressing the early release issues. I mean, look for yourself at these pictures taken with the native camera app. Do you see anything wrong? No! It takes incredible shots. If you are on ATT and shopping for an unlocked phone that is truly great, look no further than the Essential PH 1. Nuff said.

We're reviewing it all wrong... Its just the beginning.. Previously a Pixel XL user; I find the build quality, fit and finish, to be superior in all respects. (The manufacturing tolerances must be measured in the .001 range.) It is impressive under magnification. True, the Camera and its supporting software is only average when compared to any other stock Android experience, but Essential has proven their commitment by promptly updating the device firmware to resolve initial release issues. Just using the Pixel Camera App improved picture quality substantially. Think of the Essential PH-1 as the new Sony PlayStation 5, rushed to the public with only 1 or two game titles, Pong being one of them; yes, it would disappointment, but given time to refine and update the release of new software and it will blow everything out of the water because the Hardware is "there"...

Beware of Essential and how it does business. I am extremely disappointed in the Essential PH-1 phone and the company's support model. I bought the PH-1 phone from Amazon who only sells it via third party resellers as Essential the company does not directly sell their phone through Amazon. Within two weeks, the PH-1 camera stops working so I contacted Essential for support. Keep in mind that Essential sells phones but does not have a phone number to contact them for support. They only communicate through email. I describe the problem to them and they request additional information from me: my name, address, proof of purchase, serial number, etc. After providing them with all the data, they inform me that they will not support me because I bought the phone from a reseller. They said they only support the phone if it is bought directly from Essential and Amazon.

Best User Experience! Visionary Phone with Amazing Value and Out-of-this-world Build Quality. I was eyeing the Essential phone ever since it was announced. Now, after the price drop, it's almost a no-brainer. If you look at the hardware specifications alone, you don't do this phone justice. Sure, there is no heart-rate monitor, no iris scanner, no wireless charging, not even a headphone jack. It's not an OLED display, there is no optical image stabilization (OIS), no telephoto or wide-angle lens. But there is also no Bixby button, no pre-installed proprietary calendar / app store / file browser bloatware, no screwing around with basic android functionality. Not unlike the Pixel, Nexus, and old Moto phones under Google's control, the Essential PH-1 is about user experience. The Essential PH-1 looks not as sleek as some other flagships, but somehow you want to pick it up and interact with it. Why? It is not annoying.
